sections.section_title: Background: Immune-Mediated Necrotising Myopathy and GLP-1 Receptor Agonists
sections.description: This section provides the essential background knowledge needed to understand the case. It covers the definition and pathophysiology of IMNM, its serologic markers, and the paradigm of drug-induced IMNM using the statin model. It also introduces GLP-1 receptor agonists, their mechanisms, indications, and previously reported muscle-related adverse effects.
subtopics: Definition and diagnostic criteria for immune-mediated necrotising myopathy (IMNM)
Pathophysiologic features: necrotising myofibres, paucity of lymphocytic infiltrates, and complement-mediated injury
Key autoantibodies: anti-HMGCR and anti-SRP antibodies, and significance of seronegative cases
Drug-induced IMNM: lessons from statin-associated autoimmune myopathy
GLP-1 receptor agonists: mechanism of action, approved indications, and common adverse effects
Previously reported muscle toxicity with GLP-1 agonists: rhabdomyolysis case with tirzepatide

sections.description: This section details the systematic diagnostic approach used in this case, explaining the rationale for each investigation and how findings were interpreted. It covers laboratory studies, imaging, and the critical role of muscle biopsy in establishing the diagnosis. The differential diagnosis process distinguishes IMNM from toxic myopathy and idiopathic autoimmune myositis.
subtopics: Laboratory evaluation: CK elevation, transaminases, and myositis-specific autoantibody panel
Interpretation of seronegative status in the context of IMNM
Imaging studies: MRI of bilateral femurs and findings of muscular edema
Cardiac evaluation: echocardiogram and cardiac MRI findings
Muscle biopsy technique and histopathologic findings: necrosis, regeneration, CD68+ macrophages, and membrane attack complex deposition
Differential diagnosis: distinguishing IMNM from rhabdomyolysis, toxic myopathy, and other inflammatory myopathies
Key diagnostic reasoning: features supporting drug-induced IMNM versus idiopathic IMNM

sections.description: This section explains the therapeutic approach and the reasoning behind treatment decisions. It discusses the rationale for aggressive immunosuppression, the specific medications used, and the monitoring of response. The section also addresses important considerations such as steroid tapering and avoidance of GLP-1 receptor agonists.
subtopics: Rationale for aggressive immunosuppression in severe IMNM
Intravenous methylprednisolone pulse therapy: dosing and duration
Role of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) in refractory or severe IMNM
Transition to oral prednisone and tapering strategy
Monitoring treatment response: CK trends and functional improvement
Importance of drug withdrawal and continued avoidance of GLP-1 receptor agonists
Management of complications: septic shock during immunosuppression

sections.section_title: Clinical Outcomes, Lessons, and Pharmacovigilance Implications
sections.description: This section covers the patient's clinical outcome and follow-up, comparing it to the expected course of idiopathic IMNM. It discusses the causality assessment methodology used to link semaglutide to IMNM, and highlights the clinical lessons learned. The section emphasizes the importance of pharmacovigilance given the widespread use of GLP-1 receptor agonists.
subtopics: Clinical outcome: functional recovery and normalization of CK
Comparison of disease course to typical idiopathic IMNM requiring prolonged immunosuppression
Cardiac function recovery on follow-up imaging
WHO-Uppsala Monitoring Centre causality assessment criteria applied to this case
Clinical lessons: recognizing drug-induced IMNM and distinguishing it from direct toxic effects
Pharmacovigilance implications for GLP-1 receptor agonists
Future directions: need for additional case reports and predisposing factor identification
